context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: Implement the validated design at lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md: wrap each of Poller's six sequential per-tenant operations in a Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)/release/1 pair, skip-and-log on {:error, :capacity}, and write tests covering all REQ-218 acceptance criteria with mutation-testing verification.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), a tick over 3 tenant schemas calls Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 ZERO times for any of them (each skipped for capacity), the GenServer does not crash, and the next tick (cap restored) resumes normally -- verified by a test asserting the mock/spy call count is exactly 0 during the forced-zero tick and exactly 3 on the following tick

with the global cap forced to admit exactly 1 concurrent unit, a tick still processes all 3 tenant schemas' timer poll-and-fire loop to completion (sequential acquire/release, not a permanent block), confirmed by observing all 3 schemas' poll_and_fire/1 calls occur within that single tick

an admission {:error, :capacity} for one schema's operation within a tick does not prevent a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation, or that SAME schema's OTHER operations, from being attempted later in the same tick -- explicit test forcing capacity exhaustion mid-tick and observing partial, not total, skip

Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, _}) is never called anywhere in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- grep-verified, confirming decision 3's per-tenant-exclusion is actually implemented, not just described

an existing per-operation rescue path (e.g. maybe_run_alert_detection/3's rescue _ -> :ok) still catches its own operation's raise with the new acquire/release wrapped around it -- a test forcing that operation to raise still leaves the admission slot released (no leak) and the tick completes
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Implemented per lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md exactly: added a private with_admission/3 helper in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex that wraps each of the six named per-schema operations (timer poll-and-fire loop; retention sweep; alert detection; ordering cycle; ordering sweeper; ordering metrics) in an acquire/release pair against Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global) -- {:ok, ref} -> try do fun.() after Admission.release(ref) end (the existing rescue for rows 3-6 lives INSIDE fun.(), unchanged, so the acquire/release wraps around it as a whole, exactly per the design's §1); {:error, :capacity} -> Logger.warning(...) naming both schema and operation, then falls through to the next schema -- no crash, no total-tick skip. maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 (REQ-194) is left UNWRAPPED per the design's own §7 Q1 resolution (not one of the six named operations). Only :global is ever acquired -- grep-verified (see AC4 below), matching decision 3 (Poller never uses the per-tenant semaphore). No change to Letflow.Application's supervision tree or to Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's own contract; the wrap is entirely at the poller.ex call sites.

AC1's REQ-text/design-flagged 'mock/spy call count' conflict (§7 Q3): resolved per the design's own instruction -- no mocking library exists in this codebase (confirmed via mix.exs, matching poller_test.exs's own established convention), so AC1 is verified via a REAL effect assertion (due timers' actual fired/pending status), not a spy call count.

TESTS WRITTEN (test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs, 6 new describe blocks, all real DB / real Letflow.Admission singleton via test/support/admission_test_helpers.ex's restart_admission!/1, reused unmodified):
- AC1: restart_admission!(pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 2) (global_cap == 1), hold the sole unit externally before a tick over 3 schemas with due timers -- all 3 remain pending (real-effect zero-calls proof); release the probe and run a second tick -- all 3 fire.
- AC2: same cap == 1, no probe held, one tick over 3 schemas -- all 3 fire within that single tick (sequential acquire/release drains without permanent block).
- AC3: a genuine partial (not total) skip within one tick requires an actual concurrent contender racing for the sole unit (a single sequential caller like Poller never contends with itself -- confirmed structurally in §3 of the design). Implemented an antagonist Task that continuously acquires-then-releases the sole global unit throughout the tick, run against 10 schemas, retried up to 5 times (nondeterministic which specific attempts collide) until a genuine mixed outcome (some fired, some not) is observed -- this is a real race against the actual admission decision, not a simulated one.
- AC4: static source-text grep asserting lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex contains no "{:tenant," substring anywhere (including the moduledoc prose, which I had to reword once during implementation to avoid a false positive against my own documentation).
- AC5: forces a real raise inside maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1 (and _sweeper/1, _metrics/1, which share the same effect_completions table) by dropping ONLY that table from an otherwise fully-provisioned, fully-migrated tenant schema -- poll_and_fire and retention are unaffected (their own tables remain intact), isolating the fault to exactly the ordering rows this AC is about. Asserts the tick completes without crashing, a different (intact) schema's own operations still succeed in the same tick, and a post-tick try_acquire(:global) succeeds under global_cap == 1 (proving no leaked ref).
- AC6: verified via the compile/test commands below (not a separate test case).

REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING TEST DEVELOPMENT (not anticipated, discovered via mutation testing): my first AC5 draft used a Registration row pointing at a schema_name for which CREATE SCHEMA was never run at all (a 'ghost' schema). Two real defects surfaced:
1. TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 calls Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto) as its own first step, which rolls back the still-open Letflow.DataCase {:shared, self()} transaction my earlier ghost-registration insert had run under -- silently discarding it. The AC5 test was PASSING for the wrong reason (the ghost schema was never actually in the tenant list Poller iterated, so no raise was ever exercised) -- caught only because the task's mutation-testing discipline (narrowing maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1's rescue clause + moving admission release out of its after clause) still passed, which should have been impossible if the fault injection were real. Fixed the helper to call Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto) itself first and added explicit on_exit/1 cleanup (a real, uncommitted-nothing commit needs real teardown, not rollback).
2. Separately, and more importantly for scope: a schema missing its Postgres schema ENTIRELY (not just one table) makes Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 itself raise (Postgrex undefined_table on the timers table) -- contradicting this module's own moduledoc claim that poll_and_fire/1's contract already guarantees it never raises. Since poll_and_fire (row 1) has NO poller-side rescue by design (that contract is supposed to make one unnecessary), this raise is NOT isolated -- it crashes the entire tick before ever reaching the ordering rows AC5 is actually about. This is a pre-existing gap in poll_and_fire/1's own raise-safety contract, NOT something REQ-218 introduces or is scoped to fix (REQ-218 adds no rescue to row 1, matching the design's own table). Switched the AC5 fault injection to drop only the ordering-specific effect_completions table from an otherwise-intact, fully-migrated schema, which avoids the pre-existing gap entirely and isolates the fault to the three ordering rows. Flagging the poll_and_fire/1 gap for REVIEWER/ORCH as a separate, out-of-scope finding worth a future issue (a tenant schema entirely missing its timers table is an unusual but not impossible state, e.g. mid-deprovisioning) -- not fixed here.

MUTATION TESTING (both done for real, both caught by the intended tests, reverted and reconfirmed after each):
1. Bypassed the capacity check entirely in with_admission/3 (always call fun.() regardless of try_acquire's result) -- AC1 and AC3 tests both genuinely failed (AC2 and the others still passed, confirming targeted, non-vacuous coverage). Reverted; reconfirmed 12/12 pass.
2. Moved Admission.release/1 out of the after clause into a plain sequential call (skipped if fun.() raises), AND narrowed maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1's rescue clause to `_e in ArithmeticError -> :ok` (so a real Postgrex.Error is not caught there) -- the AC5 test genuinely failed (crashed with the Postgrex.Error propagating all the way to the test process), exactly the leak/crash this AC guards against. Reverted both changes; reconfirmed 12/12 pass. This same mutation is also what caught the ghost-schema test bug described above on its first attempt.

COMMANDS RUN, IN ORDER, ALL IN THE FOREGROUND WITH REAL OUTPUT:
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- "Compiling 186 files (.ex)" / "Generated letflow app", zero warnings, zero errors.
2. `mix format` on lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs -- `mix format --check-formatted` on both confirms clean, no diffs.
3. `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` (isolated) -- "Result: 12 passed", run 3 times in a row with zero failures (AC3's antagonist-based test is nondeterministic in WHICH attempt succeeds, so it was specifically re-run several times standalone to confirm it never needs more than its allotted 5 retries and never fails outright).
4. `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/` -- "Result: 12 passed" (this directory contains only poller_test.exs; test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs, which covers REQ-186's other ACs, lives one level up and is unchanged by this requirement).
5. Broader sanity sweep: `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs test/letflow/obs/alerts_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/admission_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` -- "Result: 64 passed", 0 failures, no regression on any Letflow.Admission or Letflow.Obs.Alerts caller (including ISS-0429's own alert-hook-dispatch tests in this same file).

Self-review: touched process_instance.ex? No (N/A). Touched a state transition/ASCII diagram? No (N/A). Added a migration? No (N/A). This is not a tenant-data path (no new API surface, no auth, no request/response shaping) -- Poller is an internal background GenServer with no HTTP exposure, so routing to REVIEWER directly (OTP idiom/scope gate) rather than SECURITY-REVIEWER, per this task's own instruction to self-confirm that classification.
issues: Pre-existing, out-of-scope finding: Letflow.Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's moduledoc-documented 'never raises' contract does not hold for a tenant schema missing its Postgres schema entirely (raises Postgrex undefined_table on the timers table) -- discovered via an early AC5 test draft, not introduced by REQ-218 and not fixed here since row 1 has no poller-side rescue by design. Recommend a follow-up issue.
